# Summary: Studienstiftung
The Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes, initially founded in Dresden in 1925, was dissolved under National Socialism in 1934 and reestablished in Cologne in 1948. It is a prestigious German scholarship foundation offering financial and academic support to exceptionally talented bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral students. Eligibility requires full-time university study in Germany, the EU, or Switzerland, without citizenship or age restrictions. Admission pathways include nomination by schools, university professors, examination boards, competition winners, alumni, and artists; applicants undergo selection seminars and assessment tests focusing on academic excellence, social engagement, and personal motivation.
Scholarship benefits include a monthly allowance (approximately €300), health insurance subsidies, need-based funding up to €855 monthly, increased support for students with children, and doctoral scholarships with higher stipends. Academic support involves summer schools, research groups, workshops, mentoring, and funding for scholar-organized events. In 2023, about 2,179 general and 301 doctoral scholarships were awarded, representing roughly 0.48% of German students, with participation rates and scholar shares varying by university. The foundation also offers specialized programs and partnerships, such as the KAUST-Studienstiftung program for STEM scholars and collaborations in the arts. Notable alumni include several Nobel laureates, Fields Medalists, and leaders in science, social sciences, business, politics, and the arts.
